logline: Three impoverished sisters stumble onto 70 billion won linked to Korea's wealthiest family, and what begins as a financial windfall spirals into a conspiracy of inheritance, betrayal, and survival.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series, 12 episodes, concluded October 9, 2022. No continuation has been announced.

bollymeter.basis: 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics at 8.5/10 average; 7.7 IMDb from a wider audience base; APAN Drama of the Year 2023; critics praised the thriller architecture and Kim Go-eun's lead performance while audiences tracked a meaningful dip mid-series.

seasons.review_body: Directed by Kim Hee-won and written by Jeong Seo-kyung - the team behind The World of the Married - this 12-episode tvN series aired Saturdays and Sundays from September 3 to October 9, 2022, ranking first in its timeslot every week with a 11.1 percent finale rating. The 100-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 6 critics highlighted the strong ensemble, particularly Kim Go-eun's eldest-sister lead and Uhm Ji-won's antagonist, and the structural confidence of a thriller built around class and female agency. Entertainment Weekly listed it among the top 21 Korean shows on Netflix in 2025. The 7.7 IMDb score from a broader audience signals a mid-series stretch where the conspiracy mechanics get unwieldy - episodes 7 to 9 produced the lowest individual ratings - but the opening two episodes and the finale rank among the strongest hours.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere earns its 8.2 IMDb rating by grounding the fantasy-scale stakes in granular class detail: the sisters' poverty is specific and unglamorous, and the discovery that changes their lives arrives not through luck but through a combination of coincidence and action. Reviewers noted the episode's economy - a lot of world-building delivered without feeling like exposition.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Oh In-joo discovering the money - the exact instant the thriller mechanics engage and the tone shifts from domestic drama.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale - the series' highest-rated broadcast episode at 11.1 percent nationwide - attempts to pay off a conspiracy that had grown more complex than the run time could fully accommodate. Critics were divided on whether the resolution was earned, but the ensemble's final performances and the class-politics throughline received consistent praise.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The confrontation that recontextualises whose story this actually was - a structural reversal the screenplay had planted across all twelve episodes.
